topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Velocity-Position Analogy
lecture_lines: A robot moves along a straight path.
Speedometer shows instantaneous velocity at each moment.
Distance is the accumulated velocity over time.
Area under speed curve equals total distance.
Integration and differentiation link these concepts.
animations: Animate robot (color: #FFD700) moving right on a line.
Display a speedometer showing value v(t) in real time.
Show a progress bar filling up as the robot moves.
Draw the area under the velocity curve (color: #00BFFF) filling up.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Graphical Slope vs. Area
lecture_lines: Derivatives represent the slope of the tangent.
Integrals represent the area under the curve.
Both describe the same geometric function differently.
animations: Show line graph with tangent line (color: #FF4500) and label 'Slope'.
Display a shaded area under the curve (color: #32CD32) and label 'Area'.
Toggle between highlighting the slope and the area symbols.

sections.title: The Core Mechanism: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
lecture_lines: Integration reverses the process of differentiation.
Accumulation function tracks area under the curve.
Area growth rate equals the function height.
This confirms the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
It bridges local change and total accumulation.
animations: Display f(x) and its integral F(x) side-by-side.
Draw a vertical bar (color: #FFFFFF) moving from a to b.
Show the accumulated area growing as the bar moves.
Display the equation: integral from a to b of f(x) = F(b) - F(a).
Highlight the equality between integral and difference (color: #FFD700).

sections.title: Visual Synthesis: Inverse Operations
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are inverse machines.
Derivatives map a function to change.
Integration maps change back to the original.
Constant C handles the starting point.
These operations essentially cancel each other.
animations: Draw integration 'rebuilding' the area under the curve (color: #FF00FF).
Display the constant C added to the original function.

sections.title: Summary & Application Check
lecture_lines: Derivatives measure the rate of change.
Integrals measure the total accumulation.
These inverses underpin all modern science.
animations: Show a Venn diagram connecting 'Rate' and 'Accumulation'.
Animate the conversion from v(t) to d(t) on a graph.
Display the final Fundamental Theorem formula (color: #FFFF00) centrally.
